Sources used: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs on Quzhou’s dominant wheat and maize acreage and improved-seed coverage (`42万亩小麦`, `38万亩玉米`, improved varieties above 98%) https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202107/t20210720_6372348.htm ; MOA scientific fertilization guidance for North China Plain winter wheat and summer maize https://www.moa.gov.cn/gk/nszd_1/2023/202309/t20230928_6437567.htm and https://www.moa.gov.cn/govpublic/ZZYGLS/201006/t20100606_1534673.htm ; China Agricultural University Quzhou station on recent Quzhou wheat-maize demonstration yields and nitrogen use https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html ; MOA reports on Quzhou county yields and green production results https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202405/t20240514_6455372.htm and https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/bmdt/202203/t20220307_6390769.htm

As of April 17, 2026, my winter wheat is already in the field from autumn 2025, so I will stay with the local main system: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou, this is still the steadiest way for me to earn grain and cash because the land, machinery, irrigation, and my own experience all match this rotation. I will not switch to something riskier this year. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, keep fertilizer moderate instead of pushing it too hard, and manage water carefully because wheat needs the water more and Quzhou is always tight on groundwater. For wheat, I will do rotary tillage before sowing, split nitrogen between base and topdressing, irrigate three times around overwinter recovery, jointing, and grain filling if needed, and spray about three times total for weeds, aphids, and later disease control. After wheat harvest in June 2026, I will direct-seed summer maize into the stubble with no tillage, keep one irrigation in reserve for a dry spell, and do two pesticide passes if pressure shows up. I am aiming above the county average, but not at experimental-field numbers; I want a plan I can actually carry through cleanly on my own.
